To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
caffeine ingestion increased voluntary activation and strength during isometric, eccentric, and concentric contractions of the knee extensors.
caffeine increased voluntary activation and strength in the quadriceps muscle regardless of the type of contraction (isometric, concentric or eccentric).
caffeine ingestion (8 mg/kg) increased MVT during isometric, eccentric and concentric contractions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of caffeine on voluntary activation of the human quadriceps during isokinetic and isometric contraction.
the effects of caffeine on voluntary activation of skeletal muscle during different contraction modes.
the effects of caffeine intake on the voluntary activation and strength during isometric, eccentric and concentric contractions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
caffeine ingestion induces an acute increase in the voluntary activation of the muscle and thus increases voluntary strength.

caffeine ingestion increases the strength of the quadricep muscle during isometric and concentric contractions, but the increase in voluntary activation is only observed during isometric and explosive concentric contractions.
caffeine ingestion increases voluntary activation and MVT of the quadriceps regardless of the contraction type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
caffeine ingestion increases voluntary activation and strength during all three contraction modes.
caffeine ingestion induced a significant increase in voluntary activation which was responsible for the increase in voluntary strength.
caffeine ingestion induces an increase in voluntary activation, which is associated with increased MVTs regardless of contraction mode (i.e. isometric, concentrics or eccentric).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of caffeine on voluntary activation and strength are not contraction-mode specific.
caffeine can increase voluntary activation and strength in the quadriceps muscle, and these effects are independent of the contraction mode.
caffeine ingestion can enhance strength in all contraction modes, but the effect is greater in explosive strength.
